To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ability of calcium to induce exocytosis is dependent on protein kinase C, which is activated in permeabilized RBL-2 cells by calcium through the generation of diacylglyceride.

(1) in permeabilized RBL-2 cells, protein kinase (PK) C is required for calcium-dependent exocytic release of preformed granule contents; (2) the PKC isozyme alpha is responsible for the effect of PKC on exocytosis and is the major PKC isozymes translocating to the membrane in response to calcium; (3) the effect of PKCs on exocytotic release is mediated, at least partially,
protein kinase C regulates exocytosis by acting on a G protein(s).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of protein kinase Cs in the control of Ca(2+)(dependent) exocytosis.
the role of calcium and protein kinase C in exocytosis and the potential involvement of GTP-binding proteins.
the role of protein kinase c (PKC) in the regulation of exocytosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ca(2+) and protein kinase C-dependent exocytotic mechanism is not a simple one but rather a complex and intricate one, involving the activation of several proteins.
protein kinase C, through activation of a G protein, is involved in calcium-dependent excretion.
protein kinase C, which may be activated by calcium, is required for exocytotic competence in permeabilized RBL-2 cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

protein kinase C is not required for calcium-dependent exocytic secretion, but that protein kinase C can potentiate the effects of Ca2+ by activating a GTP-binding regulatory protein(s) that is required for secretion.
protein kinase C is not required for calcium-induced exocytosis but is involved in the activation of a G protein that regulates exocytosis.
protein kinase C is required for exocytotic competence and that its activation by calcium in permeabilized RBL cells involves the generation of diacylglycerols.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Ca(2+)/protein kinase C system is a major determinant in the regulation of exocytosis.
the role of PKC in the regulation of exocytosis is not as straightforward as it might appear.
the role of protein kinase c in exocytosis is to regulate the activity of a G protein that directly controls the exocytototic machinery.
